anomalies.observed: C6 is valued 0.1mF (100uF) at 50V but uses the 0603 (C_0603_1608Metric) chip footprint. Its own extra fields describe a 0.1uF 16V X7R 0402 part, and its MPN is the 0.1uF CC0603KRX7R9BB104. A 100uF ceramic cannot fit in a 0603 package, so the value, footprint and part data disagree.
anomalies.expected: The HDMI 5V decoupling capacitor on /HDMI_5v should be a 0.1uF (100nF) ceramic in the 0603 footprint, as the part data and the other 0.1uF decoupling capacitors on this board indicate.

evidence.quote: C6 | 0.1mF 50V | Capacitor_SMD:C_0603_1608Metric | Device:C | Unpolarized capacitor | Field4=Farnell, ... Part Description=	0.1uF 10% 16V Ceramic Capacitor X7R 0402 (1005 Metric), ... MPN=CC0603KRX7R9BB104

anomalies.impact: The value is off by three orders of magnitude relative to the intended 0.1uF decoupling. A 100uF capacitor in a 0603 body is not a buildable or reliable part, so the HDMI 5V rail would lose its high-frequency decoupling or the assembled board would be built with a mismatched part.

parsed.summary: C6, the decoupling capacitor on the HDMI 5V rail, is labelled 0.1mF but sits in a 0603 footprint and carries 0.1uF part data, so its value is inconsistent with its package and role. The rest of the passive values I checked, including the LM2576 and TPS61040 feedback networks, look consistent.
